C_calculator_change_of_base.title: C: Evaluate With a Calculator (3 dp)

per_question.error_detail: Kai correctly identified that $0.001 = 10^{-3}$, but wrote the full exponential expression instead of extracting the exponent. The question asks for the value of the logarithm, which is the exponent alone: $\log_{10}(0.001) = -3$, not $10^{-3}$.
per_question.coaching: A logarithm IS the exponent. When you find $10^{-3} = 0.001$, the log is $-3$, not the whole expression $10^{-3}$. Strip away the base — the answer is just the power.

per_question.problem: Evaluate with a calculator (3 decimal places): $\log_6(12000)$
per_question.error_detail: Minor rounding issue. Kai got 5.491 instead of 5.242. The change-of-base setup was correct ($\log(12000)/\log(6)$) but the calculator execution produced an inaccurate result.
per_question.coaching: Double-check your change-of-base division on the calculator. $\log(12000) = 4.07918$, $\log(6) = 0.77815$. Divide carefully: $4.07918 \div 0.77815 = 5.242$.

per_question.problem: Evaluate with a calculator (3 decimal places): $\log_7(0.6)$
per_question.error_detail: Kai got $-0.222$ which is $\log_{10}(0.6)$, not $\log_7(0.6)$. He set up the change-of-base formula but only computed the numerator — forgot to divide by $\log(7) = 0.8451$. Correct: $\log(0.6)/\log(7) = -0.2218/0.8451 = -0.263$.
per_question.coaching: Change-of-base has TWO parts: $\log_b(x) = \log(x) / \log(b)$. You computed $\log(0.6)$ but stopped there. Always divide by $\log(\text{base})$. This is the #1 gap to fix before the unit test.

per_question.problem: Solve: $4^{x-5} = 28/3$. Give exact form and decimal (3 dp).
per_question.error_detail: Exact algebraic form is perfect. Decimal value wrong: got 5.873 instead of 6.611. $\log_4(28/3) = \log(9.333)/\log(4) = 0.9700/0.6021 = 1.611$. Then $5 + 1.611 = 6.611$. Kai likely made a calculator input error on $\log_4(28/3)$.
per_question.coaching: Your algebra is excellent — exact form was spot-on. The decimal error is a calculator execution issue. Tip: compute $\log(28/3)$ and $\log(4)$ separately, write both down, THEN divide. Don't try to do it in one calculator chain.

per_question.problem: Town population: $P(t) = 8000 \cdot (1.03)^t$. (a) What was the initial population?
Radioactive decay: $A(t) = 500 \cdot (0.85)^t$ grams after $t$ years. (a) What fraction remains after 1 year?
(b) When will the sample decay to 50 grams?
per_question.error_detail: Got 17.887 instead of 14.164. The setup $500 \cdot (0.85)^t = 50$ → $(0.85)^t = 0.1$ → $t = \log(0.1)/\log(0.85)$ is correct conceptually but the calculator division produced the wrong result. $\log(0.1) = -1$, $\log(0.85) = -0.07058$. $t = -1 / -0.07058 = 14.164$.
per_question.coaching: Minor calculator error. The algebra and setup are correct. Try entering $\log(0.1) \div \log(0.85)$ as two separate calculations and dividing the results.
